newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's bourse warns investors of long transfer.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's bourse warns investors of long transfer.

text.p: Croatia's central bourse, the Zagreb Stock Exchange, on Tuesday warned investors to inquire into the length of administrative procedures that hold up trading, but said it was working on a way to speed it up.
"The procedure of the (share) titles transfer in companies which are not listed in the first and second quotation...takes too long," it said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
It also cautioned potential buyers to calculate with longer settlement than the seven days, set by its rules.
Croatia still has no central register of shares that could simplify the process of share transfer to new owners.
These problems are seen as major obstacles to developing a liquid stock market which could attract more foreign investors to prop it up in the absence of domestic cash.
The bourse said it was preparing a "temporary solution for clearing and settlement", which should act as a bridge until all market infrastructure is properly established.
It did not say when this could be put to work.
Spokesman Zeljko Kardum said there were no problems with a timely share transfer and settlement in two fully-listed firms -- Pliva pharmaceuticals and Zagrebacka Banka.
But other firms which, which keep their individual registers of shares, because of administrative hold-ups often drag out this procedure, he pointed out.
For the moment the Zagreb Stock Exchange, with a handful of liquid issues, is used only for secondary trading and not for primary issue of shares but this is likely to change.
"Consequences which may arise when companies seek to raise capital through the market are difficult to foresee," the bourse added. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
